name: quiche
description: 🥧 Savoury implementation of the QUIC transport protocol and HTTP/3
one_liner: Low-level plumbing code that lets computers talk to each other faster over the internet using a newer, quicker version of the technology behind HTTPS.
buyer: There isn't a realistic non-technical buyer here — this is internal networking infrastructure used by engineers building browsers, CDNs, or network hardware, not a product a business purchases.
business_use_cases: A CDN or edge-networking company uses it to serve web traffic faster over HTTP/3.
A hardware or telecom vendor embeds it to add modern QUIC support to a networking product.
An app with heavy mobile traffic (video, gaming) integrates it to reduce connection latency on flaky networks.

money_ideas.idea: No direct end-customer monetization path; value is captured indirectly by companies who already sell networking/CDN products.

steal_this: Honestly, there's no realistic weekend business here. This is protocol-level infrastructure for teams already building networking products, not a starting point for a new venture.
